title: Amazon Lab126 Clinic Project
text:
The Harvey Mudd College clinic program engages juniors and seniors in solving real-world, technical problems for companies and organizations. I was the team lead for Amazon Lab126’s clinic project for the 2023-2024 academic school year. Throughout the year, I lead a team of four students in a year long project to meet the requirements of the liaisons and clients. I utilized project management tools and developed team dynamics to maximize outcome performance. My team successfully simulated acoustic environments in the software tool Unity to enhance the performance of the Amazon Echo.
Duration: August 2023 - May 2024 Team Size: 5 people
Role: Team Lead

title: Motiv Electric Trucks Research and Development Intern
text:
Motiv Electric Trucks (Now under the Workhorse name) is a leading manufacturer of medium-duty commercial all-electric trucks and buses.
During the summer of 2023, I was a R&D intern where I designed charging architecture incorporating electronic and mechanical elements for AC power distribution.



Motiv render with arrows indicating location of dual power ports


During the development process, I leveraged design requirements and component library management while working on the bill of materials development. Specifically, I gained experience in the PCB design and manufacturing process working with Altium Designer.



Final PCB Before Assembly


After I had printed my design, I learned how to assemble a PCB and test it in the lab.



Testing in the Lab


At the end of my internship, I delivered a presentation of my process to the team.



Presenting Schematic to the Team

title: LAIR Machine Learning Research Intern
text: While working at the Laboratory for Autonomous and Intelligent Robotics (LAIR), I conducted research on the biomechanics of skateboarding, utilizing 3D calibration techniques to track and analyze movement in DeepLabCut. My work involved performing inverse dynamics to measure the kinematic forces exerted on joints, providing valuable insights into the physical demands of skateboarding. This research not only deepened my understanding of biomechanics but also enhanced my ability to apply advanced analytical tools to real-world applications in robotics and human movement studies.

title: CLAUDIA NANEZ
text:
About
I am a first year master’s student in the dual MA/MSc Innovation Design Engineering (IDE) program offered jointly by Imperial College London and the Royal College of Art. In May of 2024, I graduated from Harvey Mudd College with a Bachelor of Science in Engineering and a minor in Studio Art.
With a passion for combining technical innovation with creative design thinking, I bring a unique perspective to solving complex challenges at the intersection of engineering and design.
When I’m not in the studio, I love to make music, run, and be outdoors!
